evidence.observation: Newly added focused test. Setup follows the module discipline (GitTemporaryDirectory + git.Repo, a committed then dirtied file.txt, InputOutput(yes=True)), action is Coder.create(..., auto_commits=False, dirty_commits=True) followed by coder.check_for_dirty_commit(str(fname)), and assertions verify that auto_commits=False forces coder.dirty_commits False and leaves coder.need_commit_before_edits empty, while the default coder schedules the dirty file (path in need_commit_before_edits). This is a distinct command/config behavior relative to the existing config tests in the file (suggest_shell_commands, detect_urls, chat_language, system_prompt_prefix).

Shared setup/action/assertion discipline for the module: setUp builds a Model('gpt-3.5-turbo') used by every test and patches aider.io.webbrowser.open so tests stay offline and deterministic. The new test reuses this setUp and the same GitTemporaryDirectory action pattern.

Existing focused config test that constructs a Coder with a single boolean config kwarg (suggest_shell_commands=False) inside GitTemporaryDirectory and asserts the resulting coder attribute. It is the closest precedent for the new test's structure and confirms the file already hosts focused config-behavior tests.

Source of the behavior under test: when the auto_commits constructor/config argument is falsy, dirty_commits is coerced to False before self.auto_commits and self.dirty_commits are assigned, so auto_commits=False disables dirty-commit handling even if dirty_commits=True was explicitly requested.

Observable effect used by the assertions: check_for_dirty_commit returns early when self.dirty_commits is False, so a dirty file is never added to need_commit_before_edits when auto_commits/dirty_commits are off; with dirty_commits on and repo.is_dirty(path) true it appends the path to need_commit_before_edits.

claims.claim: tests/basic/test_coder.py can host a focused setup/action/assertion test for a distinct config behavior, as demonstrated by the new test_no_auto_commits_disables_dirty_commits (lines 1037-1074), which mirrors the existing pattern in test_no_suggest_shell_commands and reuses TestCoder.setUp.

The new test is grounded in real coder behavior: Coder.__init__ (base_coder.py:409-413) coerces dirty_commits to False whenever auto_commits is False, and Coder.check_for_dirty_commit (base_coder.py:2175-2189) short-circuits when dirty_commits is False, so need_commit_before_edits stays empty under auto_commits=False and contains the dirty path under the default config.

The added test is distinct from existing coverage: tests/basic/test_coder.py already tests suggest_shell_commands, detect_urls, chat_language, and system_prompt_prefix, but no test in the file exercises the auto_commits/dirty_commits interaction at the Coder attribute/behavior level.

conclusion: Added one focused test, test_no_auto_commits_disables_dirty_commits, to tests/basic/test_coder.py (lines 1037-1074) using the module's existing setup/action/assertion discipline: GitTemporaryDirectory plus a committed-then-dirtied file as setup, Coder.create with auto_commits=False/dirty_commits=True plus coder.check_for_dirty_commit as the action, and attribute plus need_commit_before_edits assertions including a default-config positive control. The test targets a distinct command/config behavior (auto_commits disabling dirty commits) grounded in aider/coders/base_coder.py:409-413 and 2175-2189. Only tests/basic/test_coder.py was modified; no task metadata, oracle files, locks, or git configuration were touched.
